comment: Bytes, measured over the **production** build, which is the one that ships and the one `gates:size` now makes for itself in reports/size/production/. A budget here moves DOWN only (AGENTS.md section 11, ADR-0003 decision 5); raising one is a commit that says why, inside the diff the reviewer reads. The byte count is no longer the only instrument over this build: scripts/gates/module-manifest.json lists which modules each bundle contains, and that list is what now catches a module arriving. || MEASURED. Set on 2026-09-13 from a production build at main.cjs 1078, preload.cjs 547, renderer.js 649, index.html 898, renderer.css 1313 — total 4485, reproduced in this lane rather than taken from the record that carried them. index.html and renderer.css are copied rather than bundled and are byte-identical in both build modes. Every number was checked against the file on disk and against esbuild's own `metafile.outputs[...].bytes`, which at the pinned esbuild 0.28.2 are equal for all three bundles in both modes; the budgets compare the file on disk, because that is what a distributable is and it stays the right quantity if esbuild ever changes what it counts. || MARGIN. Four of the five budgets are their measured size plus one kibibyte, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte, so the real margin is between 1024 and 2047 bytes per file. Under the previous weighing that margin was sized against documentation, because the development build keeps doc comments and the bound that mattered was the largest doc block in the project, RowFlag's clip-bit documentation at 1748 source bytes. **That bound is gone**: this build is minified, so a doc comment costs a bundle nothing at all and no margin has to absorb one. What the margin is sized against now is ordinary code. Measured 2026-09-13 by building each module on its own and reading its metafile attribution, one line of this project's code costs between 4.9 and 19.9 production bytes — 19.9 in src/ui/renderer.ts, 17.3 in src/app/window.ts, 13.0 in src/contracts/commit-columns.ts — so a kilobyte of margin is between 50 and 200 lines of new code, which is a slice's worth and not an edit's. What this margin does NOT catch is what it never caught: the failure it was set after, the unread contract ring returning to both shell bundles, is +76 production bytes and passes here with room to spare. That is now the module manifest's job and not this file's, and a reader who expects the byte count to see it will be wrong. || RENDERER HEADROOM, which was an initial budget until E01-M01-S07 calibrated it (comment-e01-m01-s07 below). renderer.js is a stub awaiting E01-M01-S05, so its measured 649 bytes are not a size this rule can add a margin to; the steady-state rule would give 2048, and a budget whose first act is to be raised teaches that budgets are for raising. The precedent is ADR-0002 decision 6, which sets ten budgets over an application that does not exist and says: 'These are the initial budgets. S07 of the first milestone calibrates them by measuring the assembled application on the development machine and commits the baselines.' E01-M01-S07 is budgets, baselines and render stability, and **this budget is calibrated there**, so the movement expected of it is DOWNWARD at calibration rather than upward at S05. It is not exempt from the ratchet and must not be read as though it were: if it ever has to move outward it moves in an argued commit like any other. The 12288 is derived, and here is the derivation, measured in this lane. The floor: a stand-in consumer built outside this repository that only reads the existing decode API and the flag constants — no row pool, no canvas, no markup — costs 1745 production bytes, of which 1320 are the contract modules it pulls in (commit-columns 793, refs 147, column-read 143, result 127, layout 98, bridge 21, index 0) and 425 its own body; a second stand-in that also calls the bridge and names the channels costs 2465. The rate: 19.9 production bytes per line of code, the densest of the nine modules measured above and the one that is browser-targeted renderer code. The estimate, which is an inference and is labelled as one: a renderer meeting ADR-0002 decision 5 — a fixed pool of recycled rows moved by transform, one viewport-sized canvas redrawn from the layout buffers under a coalesced animation frame, devicePixelRatio scaling, arithmetic hit-testing, and the scroll and resize handling around them — is about 500 lines of code, which at 19.9 bytes a line is 9950 bytes; 9950 above the 1320-byte floor is 11270, and the next whole kibibyte is 12288. || TOTAL. The five budgets sum to 22528 and the total is 20480, which is below that sum, and the property it buys is narrower than it used to be. It cannot be a second constraint on renderer.js: 12288 of the total is that file's initial allocation and has to stay whole, because a total that fired when S05 filled a budget S05 was given would be an unstated second renderer budget, which is exactly the trap this file was just repaired for. So the total is a second constraint on the other four. Their measured sizes sum to 3836 and their margins are 1994, 1501, 1150 and 1759; the total leaves them 8192, of which 4356 is margin, so any TWO of the four may spend their full margin at once and any three may not. When E01-M01-S07 calibrates renderer.js downward, this number comes down with it in the same commit. || WHAT THIS MEASURES, and what it stopped measuring. It measures the bundles a user would receive. Until 2026-09-13 it measured the development build in dist/, on the reasoning — which was sound when it was written, and is kept here so that a reader can check the change — that unminified is the stricter of the two measurements and needs no second build. Both halves were true. What review round 11 measured is that 'stricter' meant stricter about comments: the same three bundles are 1.9x to 2.6x larger unminified (2173 against 1078, 1402 against 547, 1215 against 649), almost all of it doc comments, and a stand-in renderer that merely reads the decode API measured 7232 development bytes against a 3072 budget in this lane — over its whole budget before a line of rendering exists, entirely from prose. A gate that prices documentation against a bundle's budget pays an author to delete it, in a project whose discipline is writing it down, and gates:contract records shapes rather than text so nothing else would have objected. Nothing ships the development build, so the budget now weighs the one that does. The measurements behind the decision are in ADR-0003 section 2, gate 11, and in docs/plan/E01-commit-graph/M01-first-graph/S01-scaffold-and-contract.md.
comment-e01-m01-s06: THREE BUDGETS MOVED, and the total by exactly the sum of their movements. All three were initial budgets in the sense ADR-0002 decision 6 uses until E01-M01-S07, the slice that measures the assembled application and commits the baselines, calibrated them (comment-e01-m01-s07 below); none was exempt from the ratchet in the meantime. || renderer.css, 3072 -> 6144. Measured 4280 production bytes on 2026-09-19 by `npm run gates:size`, which copies it unbundled and weighs the file on disk, so these are the same bytes in both build modes. The old budget was 1313 measured plus the margin rule, set over a file that was a placeholder for a window with one sentence in it; review round 14 measured it at 2978 with 94 bytes of margin left, and this slice legitimately adds a control bar, a stage and a failure view. It is reset to the measured size plus the margin rule this file already states — measured plus one kibibyte, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte — and NOT by deleting the prose at the head of the stylesheet, which is what E01-M01-S05 had to do and what the repair of this gate was for. || repository.cjs, new, 28672. Measured 26859 production bytes on the same run: it is the utility process of ADR-0002 decision 2 and it carries src/adapters/, src/core/parse/, src/core/store/, src/core/layout/ and src/core/page/, which is most of the product and none of which was in any bundle before — the three shells measured 4485 bytes between them because nothing that reads a repository had ever been built. Same margin rule: 26859 + 1024, rounded up. || main.cjs, 3072 -> 5120, by the orchestrator's ruling recorded in this lane's task on 2026-09-20. Measured 3969 production bytes by `npm run gates:size` on 2026-09-25, after this lane was rebased onto E01-M01-S09. The old budget was 1078 measured plus the margin rule, set when the whole of the main process was opening one window; this slice makes it the composition root of ADR-0002 decision 2, with a handler for every channel and the forwarding to the utility process, so that budget was a steady-state margin applied to a placeholder exactly as renderer.css's was. Same margin rule: 3969 + 1024, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte. || TOTAL, 20480 -> 54272, which is 3072 + 28672 + 2048, the sum of the three movements and nothing else. What it still buys is what it bought before: it is a second constraint on the files whose own margins are not load-bearing, since the six file budgets now sum to 56320 and the total is 2048 below that.
comment-e01-m01-s07: CALIBRATED, AND NOTHING MOVED. The four budgets the two comments above called initial — renderer.js, renderer.css, main.cjs and repository.cjs — were measured by E01-M01-S07 with `npm run gates:size` on 2026-09-28, production build, at the lane's base ca4bab6 and again at its head, which changes nothing under src/ or scripts/build.js: renderer.js 10942 bytes, renderer.css 4280, main.cjs 3969, repository.cjs 27367 (and preload.cjs 631, index.html 898; 48087 in all). The margin rule this file states — measured plus one kibibyte, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte — gives 12288, 6144, 5120 and 28672, which is each budget's existing number, so no budget moves and the total moves by the sum of the movements, zero, and stays 54272. None of the four is labelled initial any more: each is a budget set by the margin rule over a measured size, and moves down only. Review round 14's figures for renderer.js — the contract ring at 1485 bytes and the renderer's own seven modules at 6616, measured at 0ccbd45 — are review round 14's; this calibration did not need them and did not reproduce them. || WHAT A BUILD CHANGE WOULD BUY, measured and not made. renderer.css is copied, not minified, so its comments ship: the same file with its comments removed is 3588 bytes, and the rule would give it 5120, a kibibyte under today's budget. Shipping it without them is a change to scripts/build.js, outside E01-M01-S07's boundary, and is raised rather than made.
